extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of philosophy (general educated audience)
extracted.subtask_description: A translated monograph (Henri Bergson's Creative Evolution) that sets out a method for philosophically understanding life and knowledge, critiques mechanistic and teleological accounts, and develops concepts such as real duration and the nature of consciousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Join theory of knowledge and theory of life
rubrics_metrics.description: Theory of knowledge and theory of life should be inseparable: a theory of life unaccompanied by a criticism of knowledge will be forced to accept pre-existing concepts; a theory of knowledge that does not place the intellect in the general evolution of life will not explain how frames of knowledge were constructed or how to extend them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both inquiries must join and, by a circular process, push one another on unceasingly; together they can more surely solve philosophical problems by showing the formation of the intellect and the genesis of the matter our intellect maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critique ready-made categories (mechanism and finality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not accept mechanism and teleology as given 'garments' for explaining life without testing their fit; both are 'ready-made' conceptual frameworks of the understanding that must be tried on evolutionary progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine how each mold (mechanism, finality) handles concrete biological phenomena; recut or modify the one that fits less badly rather than forcing inappropriate conceptual categories onto living processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer a method that follows generation and growth (true evolutionism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject the 'false evolutionism' of cutting up present reality into already-evolved fragments and recomposing it; instead follow reality in its generation and growth to produce a true evolutionism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philosophical reconstruction must attempt to follow the evolutionary movement itself rather than reconstructing it solely from present end-states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophy as collective, progressive work
rubrics_metrics.description: Philosophy of this kind (uniting life and knowledge) will not be produced instantly by a single genius but built up by the collective and progressive effort of many thinkers and observers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The work should aim to define the method and allow glimpses of application on essential points, expecting successive improvement and correction by others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account must recognize 'real duration' (continuity of conscious life)
rubrics_metrics.description: An adequate account of life must acknowledge that psychical existence is a continuous flow (real duration) in which past is continually preserved and swells into the present; states are not static, repeatable blocks but evolving, irreversible moments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid treating mental states as discrete, repeatable entities on an unchanging ego; emphasize memory as continuous retention and the irreversibility and creativity of each moment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish abstract (mathematical) time from lived duration
rubrics_metrics.description: When describing material systems, science uses an abstract time (t) of correspondences; but an account of life must treat lived duration as an absolute, qualitative flow that 'bites into' systems and involves invention and the creation of the new.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philosophical explanations of living processes should not simply transpose the mathematical/time-of-science model onto life without addressing qualitative, lived temporality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain how intellect arises from action (intellect as appendage of acting faculty)
rubrics_metrics.description: The intellect is formed by evolution as an appendage of the faculty of acting: its concepts and logic are shaped for representing relations among external things and securing action, therefore are especially adapted to inanimate solids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the functional origin of intellectual categories and their consequent limitations when applied to life; account for why intellectual knowledge is accurate for matter but ill-suited to present the full meaning of life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely solely on conceptual thought to reconstruct life
rubrics_metrics.description: Pure conceptual or speculative thought alone is incapable of presenting the true nature of life; the intellectual form is an emanation of life and cannot fully embrace its generating process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philosophical method must supplement conceptual thought with a discipline that opens to the other forms of consciousness and the 'nebulosity' surrounding the intellect, so as to approach life more directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for unpredictability and creative novelty in living states
rubrics_metrics.description: An account of conscious life must allow that each moment is in some sense original and unforeseeable, even though it is explained by prior elements; lived moments are simple wholes that cannot be fully predicted by projecting past elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philosophical and scientific explanations should respect the irreducible novelty present in the creation of each lived state and avoid deterministic reconstructions that deny this originality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize living bodies as true individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike most material objects that are relative to perception and isolable systems, living bodies are separated and closed off by nature herself: composed of unlike parts completing each other and performing diverse interdependent functions, i.e., true individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Biological and philosophical accounts must reflect the natural unity and integrative individuality of living organisms, not simply treat them as arbitrary divisions of matter for convenient study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translator's fidelity and preservation of style
rubrics_metrics.description: In translation: follow the text closely and preserve the 'living union of diction and thought'; aim to render difficult words/phrases with appropriate English equivalents and keep the spirit of the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translator notes that professor revised whole work; translator acknowledges help from others who weighed each word phrase by phrase—good translation practice includes careful revision, consultation, and preserving both thought and diction.
